findings.element: state=publish — the whole screen, and the Publish control in the owner bar that reaches it
findings.problem: This is the one state with an explicit emotional mandate written into its own kicker — THE MOMENT IT BECOMES THEIRS — and driving it, no moment occurs. Pressing Publish on a plan whose own status line already reads 'Live since 15 July' performs no act: the surface swaps instantly to a two-column utility pane holding a preview thumbnail, a 43-character token in a mono field, a Copy button, and a mono aside conceding SENDING COMES NEXT. Nothing is committed, nothing changes state, nothing is handed to anyone, and the bottom half of the window is empty. Every other screen in the chain knows what it is for; this one is a settings panel wearing a headline. It is also the screen an owner is in at the highest-feeling second of their use of the product — the second they give the thing away — and it gives them a clipboard.
findings.fix: Make Publish an act with a before and an after, and split the two cases the fixture already distinguishes. (a) Not yet live: label the control 'Hand it over'; pressing it composes the unfurl card out of the page the owner is looking at — the count, the date and the day's name settling into the card's geometry over 0.22s on cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), no scale and no bounce — and lands on a single line of voice type stating what just happened and to whom, 'Mara & Finn can open this now.', with the link and Copy beneath it and the status line now reading 'Live since 16 July' as a true fact rather than a preset. (b) Already live: the same route leads instead with 'They have had this since 15 July', the primary control is Copy the link, and no ceremony replays — a ceremony performed twice for one event is theatre and costs more than it earns. Keep SENDING COMES NEXT; honesty about the unbuilt half is the right call and should stay.

findings.element: owner editor · the WHEN input (input#b-edit-date) against the −7/−1/+1/+7 steppers directly beneath it
findings.problem: Drive it: open the editor on 'Send the invitations', press +7. The row slides down the measure to 30, the readout under the steppers becomes 'Saturday 15 August 2026 · in 30 days', the row's own date line becomes Sat 15 Aug, the undo bar says 'moved 7 days later' — and the field labelled WHEN, sitting one line above the buttons that caused all of it and inside the same bordered group, still says '8 August 2026'. Press −1 and it still says 8 August. The panel is now stating two different dates for one moment, and the one it states in the largest, most authoritative, most editable place is the wrong one. Nothing is corrupted — reopening the editor shows the true date — so this is not a data bug, it is a credibility bug, and it is the exact class the defect library names: every fact on the surface deriving from one accessor. It also breaks the direction's own promise that editing is moving something nearer, because the control group visibly disowns its own effect.
findings.fix: Route the field's value through the same accessor the readout and the row already use, and rewrite it on every stepper press in the same frame the item moves — set input.value from the committed date, not from the value the field was seeded with when the editor opened. Suppress the rewrite only while the field itself holds focus and its value differs from the committed one, so a half-typed date is never yanked out from under the typist, and rewrite it on blur. No other change to the panel.

findings.element: state=phone and state=desk — the received artifact, and the loading state that hands off to it
findings.problem: The whole motion vocabulary of this master is seven transitions and zero keyframes; six of the seven are hover and press background colours, and the seventh — top on .b-item — is the only compositional one and fires only when an owner presses a stepper. That single motion is the best thing in the artifact: press +7 and the moment you are planning physically retreats down the measure, which is the direction's thesis made physical. But it belongs to the owner. The audience — the couple, the families, the venue, the people the brief says will judge the whole company by one screen — never sees a single thing move. They open the link, the skeleton promises 'Bringing in what is ahead', and the finished page arrives in one hard paint. The sender's own words in the unfurl are 'It updates itself'; the received screen offers no evidence whatsoever that it is alive rather than a screenshot. A poster is a defensible answer for print. This is a link that claims to be live.
findings.fix: Spend one more motion, on the guest's first paint only. When the data lands, draw the rail from the today mark downward over 0.22s on cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) and let each item's mark and row arrive as the rail passes it, stagger 0.08s, capped so the last row is settled inside 0.3s total; opacity and the existing top only — no scale, no translate on the type, nothing that overshoots. The count, the date and the day's name paint at full strength from frame one and never animate: the horizon is the fact that must not appear to arrive. Every value in it is already inside the declared duration and easing ladders, and the existing reduced-motion block that strips every transition strips this too.

findings.element: owner editor · the reversibility bar (.b-undo) at the top of .b-editHost, at every width
findings.problem: Open the editor on any item at any width and the first thing in it is roughly 90px of nothing: the undo bar is correctly reserved in real layout and correctly made inert, but it is inert by visibility:hidden, so it holds 50px plus its margins of dead air above WHAT IT IS with no mark, no rule and no word in it. On the 390 sheet that void is the top tenth of the sheet and the eye lands in it before it lands on the moment being edited; at 1280x900 it sits immediately under the panel's top border and reads as a rendering failure. The band is right and the reservation is right; a discerning stranger does not know that, and sees a panel that opens broken.
findings.fix: Keep the band reserved and give it something true to hold at rest: when there is nothing on the stack, set .b-undoText to the moment's own committed date in mono at 12 against the 0.46 step — the same string the readout carries — so the band reads as a status line that later becomes a way back. Drop visibility:hidden from .b-undo and apply it only to .b-undoAct and its Ctrl Z hint, which stay hidden and disabled. The band's height then never changes and nothing below it moves when the first change lands.

findings.element: state=day — the folded past sentence under BEHIND YOU · 9 moments
findings.problem: The morning screen earns its keep: Today at the top of the ramp, the date, and 'This is the day the plan was for.' is the one sentence in the artifact that is written rather than specified. Then the page closes, as its final line of content on the wedding morning, on 'Venue walk-through, 19 September.' The folded-past sentence names the most recent past moment, which is exactly right on all seventy-eight other days and exactly wrong on this one. The last thing the composition says to a couple on the morning of their wedding is a note about a fortnight-old site visit.
findings.fix: On the day state only, have the folded past sentence name the FIRST moment in the record rather than the most recent one, in the grammar it already uses: 'It began on 2 January, when you said yes.', derived from the earliest past item in fixture.js through the accessor that sentence already calls. The count under BEHIND YOU stays 9 and the + still opens all nine in order, so nothing is hidden and no fact changes — only which of them the morning chooses to say out loud.

biggestWin: There is a memorable moment and it is a real one: open the owner's editor, press +7, and the moment physically retreats down the measure while the number of days it is away climbs — the direction's whole claim, that distance is the organising object, made into something you feel in your thumb rather than something you read. Around it sits a body of work that survives a sceptical stranger. The phone screen leads with 79 at 96px, the date, the day's name and 'Kept by Orla' and nothing else, and it is genuinely beautiful. The brand-new project asks one question, 'When is the day?', takes one answer, and the count is born. The print keepsake is a page a person would keep. The ended link is kind and refuses to claim a cause it cannot know. The loading state promises only what will really render. Ink and paper are both fully built rather than one being a filter over the other, and eleven states hold one voice. The distance to 9.5 is not craft and it is not polish — the craft is largely there. It is that the one moment this work has belongs to the owner, while the audience the brief says decides everything gets a static poster and a copy button. Two builds close it: give publish an act with a before and an after, and give the received artifact one arrival. Roughly a week of work, and the language for both is already declared in the lock.
